findings.title: enableSqlExpressions computes an inverted, unused flag value
findings.body: `enableSqlExpressions` assigns `enabled := !h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(featuremgmt.FlagSqlExpressions)` — i.e. the variable named `enabled` is true when the feature toggle is OFF — and then returns `false` on both branches, so the toggle lookup is dead code. The net effect (always disabled) is what this PR intends, but the function is misleading: anyone later re-enabling the feature by changing the body to `return enabled` would enable SQL expressions exactly when the toggle is disabled and disable them when it is enabled. If the intent is to hard-disable regardless of the toggle, the function should simply return false (or be a constant) without the inverted lookup; if the toggle should be honored later, the negation must be removed.

findings.title: Legacy SQL command path is only disabled implicitly via the stub error
findings.body: The explicit "sqlExpressions is not implemented" guard was added only to `ExpressionQueryReader.ReadQuery`. The legacy path (`UnmarshalSQLCommand` → `NewSQLCommand`, used by the rawNode/`buildCMDNode` flow for dashboards and alerting) has no such guard and is disabled only because `sql.TablesList` now calls a stub that returns "not implemented". That works today but has two downsides: (1) the user-facing error is `sql-invalid-sql` / "error reading SQL command", which wrongly suggests their SQL is malformed rather than that the feature is disabled, and the full raw SQL is logged at Warn level for every attempt; (2) the disablement depends on the stub remaining unimplemented — if `pkg/expr/sql/db.go` is ever filled in again, this path becomes live without any feature-toggle or defense-in-depth check. Add an explicit early return in `NewSQLCommand`/`UnmarshalSQLCommand` (or in the TypeSQL case of `buildCMDNode`) with a clear "disabled" message.

findings.title: No tests cover the new disabled behaviour; existing DuckDB-backed tests not updated
findings.body: The PR replaces the DuckDB engine with a stub whose every method returns "not implemented", and adds an unconditional rejection in `ReadQuery` for `QueryTypeSQL`, but adds no test asserting that a SQL expression query is rejected on either the reader path or the `UnmarshalSQLCommand`/`NewSQLCommand` path. Any existing tests in `pkg/expr/sql` (e.g. parser tests exercising `TablesList`) or `pkg/expr` that previously relied on the real DuckDB implementation returning table lists/frames are not modified in this PR and will now fail (or were already skipped and thus silently prove nothing). For a security hard-disable, a regression test that fails if SQL expressions become executable again is important so the fix cannot be accidentally reverted.

findings.title: FlagSqlExpressions feature toggle remains registered and documented but can never enable the feature
findings.body: After this change, SQL expressions are rejected unconditionally ("sqlExpressions is not implemented") regardless of the `sqlExpressions` feature toggle. The toggle remains in the feature registry and in the feature-toggle docs with no indication that it is now inert, so operators who enable it will get an error with no explanation. Either the toggle description/docs should state that the feature is disabled pending a secure re-implementation, or the toggle should be removed/marked as such, so users are not misled into thinking the flag still gates a working feature.
